dedupe_keys.name: ego cross grid level electricity grid and storage optimisation tool open ego project

description: eGo is the cross-grid-level electricity grid and storage optimisation tool of the open_eGo project (Open Electricity Grid Optimization). The project website read on 2026-09-26 says the aim was a transparent grid planning tool across voltage levels to investigate economically viable grid expansion scenarios, considering flexibility options such as storage and redispatch, for a German grid run by more than 800 operators. The eGo README says it integrates optimisation of flexibility options and grid extension based on the eTraGo transmission and eDisGo distribution tools, with copyright held by Europa-Universität Flensburg, Flensburg University of Applied Sciences, the DLR Institute of Networked Energy Systems and the Reiner Lemoine Institut. Coverage is Germany. All code is published on GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3, and input data and results are published on the OpenEnergy Platform, mostly under the Open Database License. Caveats: the open_eGo project has ended, and the current maintenance of eGo was not confirmed; newer data for the eTraGo and eDisGo tools is built by the eGon-data pipeline. Simulation uses are optimisation of grid expansion and flexibility across grid levels, capacity planning and power flow studies for the German energy transition. Related records: data-egon-data is the follow-up data pipeline feeding eTraGo and eDisGo, and model-pypsa is an open power system library for comparison.
